Traditional Vietnamese Dishes with Room for Improvement
Jun 2026 • Solo
First, I got the Vietnam mini pancakes (Bánh khọt), which had a crispy exterior and soft batter. They were light and not oily, making them very satisfying to eat. Next, I tried the stuffed snail with minced pork (Ốc bươu nhồi thịt hấp sả). The dish was fragrant with lemongrass, and the snails were tender while the minced pork filling was juicy. However, it lacked flavor overall and it was a bit dull. I also ordered the corn cake with green onion oil sauce (Bánh bắp). The cake was chewy and slightly dense, and I could still taste the natural sweetness of the corn. Unfortunately, it was a bit greasy. The vegetables and herbs served alongside these dishes were fresh and complemented the food well. Lastly, I had the sweet Vietnamese soup (Sâm bổ lượng). The sweetness was balanced and it contained a good variety of ingredients, but I found it somewhat underwhelming and not particularly satisfying as a dessert.

Great place for a private function
Aug 2018 • Friends
Had a party here for 8 people. We got a table on the rooftop balcony by ourselves. The restaurant is nicely decorated with the 1970s Vietnamese style that will catch your attention when you first walk in. The rooftop itself is full of plants which makes you feel like sitting in a garden with fresh air.

The food was authentic and well-done. Seafood dishes were fantastic, particularly the "ground crabs hotpot" and "stuffed snail with minced pork and lemongrass". The desserts are also recommended, namely the glass jelly and lotus sweet soup.

The price is very reasonable. We spent 3 million VND (around 130 USD) for 8 people and had more than we could eat and drink, so that is definitely cheaper compared to most places in the city centre.

The only minus point is that the balcony is on the 3rd floor so the food delivery was a bit slow.
